why: The single write-door accepts a record no reader can read, silently — so a malformed record of truth becomes permanent and surfaces only as a red in a different component.

cleared_by.what_changed: A shape gate inside append_entry (cairn/charter/projector.py): the door now REFUSES any record missing `standing`, before any file is touched. The required set is universal and is exactly one field — measured, not chosen: standing is at 98% adoption across 14 histories / 66 records, and the single record lacking it is this trouble's own occurrence; gate at 80% would have retroactively invalidated 13 legitimate records. Per-component declared shape is FILED, not built — zero consumers today. Ratified by Akien 2026-07-25. PAID FOR ITSELF IMMEDIATELY: it refused cairn/base/transitions.py::emit, which journaled no `standing` at all and had not yet written to any live history — the same silent-accept fault, caught before it became permanent. Proofs: test_append_door_instrument.py 12/12 (4 new for the gate), test_transitions.py 11/11 (2 new). Full suite 31/31 green.

occurrences.identity: cairn/charter/projector.py::append_entry — the single write-door for every component's history
occurrences.expected: A record entering a record of truth conforms to the shape that history's readers require — here, a 'standing' field, which every prior record in cairn/diagnostic_inspector/history.json (seq 0-3) carries and which harbor_master's register reads to derive a boat's standing.
occurrences.actual: The door accepted a record carrying 'id'/'what'/'why' and NO 'standing' (seq 4), wrote it to history, and returned a successful state. No error, no warning, no held diagnostic. The malformed record became permanent (Law 7 — history is append-only, so it cannot be edited out).
occurrences.fatality: non-fatal to the door, LOUD downstream — test_harbor_register.py::test_fleet_queries_both_berths_nonempty went red with 'diagnostic_inspector: a boat with no standing — the register did not read its cursor'. The whole 29-proof suite was the detector; nothing at the door itself objected.
occurrences.trace: projector.append_entry(history_path, state_path, record) -> append(history, record) [no validation] -> _atomic_write(history_path) -> project(history) -> _atomic_write(state_path) -> return state [success]. Later: harbor_master.registry reads state.json cursor -> cursor.get('standing') -> None -> assertion failure.

the_defect: The append door is the SINGLE write-door precisely so that a rule can be enforced in one place (Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy). It enforces append-only and it enforces the window bound. It enforces NOTHING about the record's shape. So the one gate that could make record-of-truth conformance structural instead lets any dict through, and a bad record is discovered — if ever — by a reader failing much later, in a different component, with a message that describes the symptom rather than the cause.
why_it_is_a_trouble_and_not_just_a_bug: It failed SILENTLY at the point of the fault. Under Akien's rule, a write that cannot be read is exactly the class of thing that must escalate rather than succeed quietly. It also violated Law 7 in the direction that is hardest to undo: the record of truth is permanent, so a silent accept means a permanent malformity, correctable only by appending a correction beside it (which is what was done — cairn/diagnostic_inspector/history.json seq 5).
resolution_so_far: The malformed seq 4 was corrected by APPEND (seq 5, carrying the required 'standing' plus a 'correction_of': 4 pointer), never by edit. The suite is green again. The DOOR is unfixed — that is what this trouble is for.
the_fix_when_taken: A schema gate inside append_entry: the door validates the record against the shape that history's readers require, and REFUSES a non-conforming write loudly rather than accepting it quietly. Open question for the ratify: whether the required shape is universal across all component histories or declared per-component (the charter would be the natural declaring surface). Not decided here — this trouble reports, it does not design.
traces_up_to: Law 4 — until the door enforces shape, conformance is policy, and this is the IOU
Law 7 — a record of truth is permanent; accepting a bad one silently is the costly direction
I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass — the fault produced no diagnostic at all at its own site
Akien's no-silent-failure rule, 2026-07-25 — the rule that made this a filed trouble rather than a fixed-and-forgotten slip
kin: cairn/diagnostic_inspector/ — the surface that will report the next one of these
found_how: Caught live, not by inspection: a real gate progression through the append door wrote a record that harbor_master's register could not read, and the failure surfaced only when a downstream proof went red.

Recipient is AKIEN, not cc: the open half is his ratify on the fix's scope, not a build.
